safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الحمد; (جاعل) a second naʿt (adjective) of the Divine Name, genitive; (رسلا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle جاعل [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) if (جاعل) is explained as meaning "Creator".]; (أولي) naʿt of (رسلا), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, as it is annexed to the sound masculine plural; (مثنى) naʿt of أجنحة, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), being a deflected adjective (ṣifa maʿdūla), and likewise (ثلاث، رباع); (في الخلق) attached to (يزيد) [Note: Or it is in the place of the second object.]; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (على كلّ) attached to (قدير).
The clause «الحمد لله ...» has no grammatical position: inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «يزيد ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله.. قدير ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of the increase: in the words of the Exalted «يَزِيدُ فِي الْخَلْقِ ما يَشاءُ»:
The best of what has been said about this verse is what al-Zamakhsharī cited in his Kashshāf: "The verse is unrestricted and covers every increase in creation: tallness of stature, well-proportioned form, completeness of limbs, strength in grip, soundness of intellect, firmness of judgement, boldness of heart, generosity of soul, fluency of tongue, elegance in speaking, fine deliberateness in handling affairs, and whatever resembles that of things description cannot encompass."

* Benefits:
1- مفعل and فعال.
From the numbers one to ten two forms are made which are diptotes, namely:
مفعل and فعال. So we say: موحد and أحاد, مثنى and ثناء, مثلث and ثلاث.. etc. The reason for their being diptotes is that these numbers are deflected adjectives (ṣifāt maʿdūla).
2- The words of the Exalted جاعِلِ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ and His words in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ فَانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ: the grammarians and exegetes said that (الواو) has the meaning of (أو), but Ibn Hishām commented on their view, saying: "This is not known in the language; it is only said by some weak parsers and exegetes." As for the verse, Abū Ṭāhir Ḥamza ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Iṣfahānī said in his book called «al-Risāla al-muʿriba ʿan sharaf al-iʿrāb»: "To say about it that the wāw means (أو) is a failure to grasp the truth. Know that the numbers that are combined are of two kinds: a kind brought so that some of it is added to some, namely the cardinal numbers (al-uṣūl), as in the words of the Exalted ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذا رَجَعْتُمْ، تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كامِلَةٌ and وَواعَدْنا مُوسى ثَلاثِينَ لَيْلَةً وَأَتْمَمْناها بِعَشْرٍ فَتَمَّ مِيقاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً; and a kind brought not so that some of it is added to some, but rather what is meant by it is separateness, not combination, namely the deflected numbers, as in the verse of al-Nisāʾ and the verse of Fāṭir just mentioned." And he said: "I.e. among them is a group possessing two wings [each], a group possessing three, three, and a group possessing four, four; so each kind is singled out with a number."

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يفتح) jussive, and given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (للناس) attached to (يفتح); (من رحمة) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (ما) [Note: Or a tamyīz (specification) of it.]; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (لها) attached to the khabar (predicate) of lā; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما يمسك فلا مرسل له) like ما يفتح.. فلا ممسك لها; (من بعده) attached to the omitted khabar [Note: The adverb is not attached to the active participle (مرسل), because the indeclinable noun of the (لا) of generic negation does not govern — this is the prevailing opinion — but with an adverb one is lenient in what one is not lenient with in other things, so there is nothing to prevent attaching it to the active participle.]; (الواو) resumptive; (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يفتح الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا ممسك لها ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «يمسك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يفتح.
The clause «لا مرسل له ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «هو العزيز ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(أنّى) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (تؤفكون), and the (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The vocative clause «يأيّها..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اذكروا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «هل من خالق غير الله..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرزقكم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) خالق.].
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تؤفكون ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if this is the truth, then how are you turned away ...
(4) - (الواو) a conjunction; (الفاء) to connect the apodosis to the condition; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (رسل) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (من قبلك) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of رسل [Note: Or attached to (كذّبت).]; (الواو) a conjunction; (إلى الله) attached to (ترجع); (الأمور) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative.
The clause «يكذّبوك..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the vocative clause.
The clause «كذّبت رسل ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «ترجع الأمور..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يكذّبوك.

safi-cedvel:5-7.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الناس) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (3) of this sūra.]; (الفاء) a conjunction to connect the effect to the cause; (لا) a jussive-governing prohibitive in both places; (تغرّنكم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa in the position of jussive, and likewise (يغرّنكم); (بالله) attached to (يغرنّكم), and (الباء) is causal, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "because of Allah's forbearance".
The clause «يأيّها الناس..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تغرنّكم الحياة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: "Take heed, and let it not deceive you ..." [Note: Or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you want to attain Allah's promise, then let not the life deceive you.].
The clause «لا يغرّنّكم بالله الغرور..» is conjoined to the clause لا تغرّنّكم الحياة ...
(6) (لكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عدو; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (عدوّا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (من أصحاب) attached to the khabar (predicate) of يكونوا.
The clause «إنّ الشيطان لكم عدوّ..» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the response to the vocative.
The clause «اتّخذوه..» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you have grasped that, then take him.. or if you want salvation from the Fire, then take him..
The clause «يدعو....» has no grammatical position: a reason for what preceded.
The clause «يكونوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the concealed particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يكونوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يدعو).
(7) (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar in both places, for the two mubtadaʾs (subjects) عذاب and مغفرة; (أجر) conjoined to مغفرة by the wāw, nominative.
The clause «الذين كفروا..» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the response to the vocative.
The clause «كفروا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لهم عذاب..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الذين كفروا ...
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «لهم مغفرة ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (الذين).

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "like one whom Allah has guided" (كمن هداه الله); (له) attached to (زيّن); (سوء) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (حسنا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi in both places; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) a jussive-governing prohibitive; (عليهم) attached to (تذهب); (حسرات) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative.], the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to عليم, with the returning pronoun omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يصنعون ...) is in the position of genitive by (الباء), attached to عليم.
The clause «من زيّن له سوء..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «زيّن له سوء..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (من).
The clause «رآه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause زيّن..
The clause «إنّ الله يضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive and causal.
The clause «يضل ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
The clause «يهدي ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يضلّ.
The clause «يشاء (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative noun (من).
The clause «لا تذهب نفسك..» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they are punished, then let not [your soul] go out ...
The clause «إنّ الله عليم..» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «يصنعون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).

* Rhetoric:
The device of al-īghāl (reinforcing supplement): in the words of the Exalted «فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَراتٍ».
The device of al-īghāl is bringing speech that serves as a completion of preceding speech, as a precaution. Allah swore by the life of the Messenger more than once that those who turned away from him and opposed him had exceeded every limit by their turning away, and showed that they were excessive in stupidity and deeply sunk in error, as the Exalted said in more than one place «لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ», and also His words «وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ»
[Translator's note: The source passage ends here without a closing sentence.]

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الفاء) a conjunction in the three places [Note: And in (سقناه) there is iltifāt (a shift) from the third person to the first person.]; (إلى بلد) attached to (سقناه); (به) attached to (أحيينا); (بعد) an adverb, accusative, attached to (أحيينا), and it is of time; (كذلك) attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (النشور).
The clause «الله الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرسل..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «تثير ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila [Note: And the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. the winds stir up by His will.].
The clause «سقناه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تثير.
The clause «أحيينا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سقناه..
The clause «كذلك النشور..» has no grammatical position: resumptive, confirming the content of what preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift): in the words of the Exalted «وَاللَّهُ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحاباً فَسُقْناهُ».
Two shifts: the first is where He reported about the past with the imperfect verb, for He said «فتثير», an imperfect, while what precedes it and what follows it is past, in order to portray the situation in which the winds stir up the clouds, and to make present that wonderful image indicating the divine power. They do this with an action that has some kind of distinction and particularity, with a state that is found remarkable, or that concerns the one addressed, or the like.
The second shift is in His words «فَسُقْناهُ إِلى بَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنا».
Had it run on the pattern of the speech, He would have said فسقى and أحيا, but He turned with them from the third-person wording to the first-person wording, which enters more into exclusiveness and indicates it more. He expressed it with two past verbs after the imperfect only to indicate certainty of occurrence.
2- The loose simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the words of the Exalted «كَذلِكَ النُّشُورُ».
A loose simile, because of the presence of the particle [of comparison], i.e. like the reviving of dead land is the resurrection of the dead, in the soundness of its being within [divine] power, or in the manner of the reviving.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (كان) a defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (لله) attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ العزّة; (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the second العزّة, i.e. in this world and the Hereafter; (إليه) attached to (يصعد); (الواو) a conjunction; (العمل) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: Or conjoined to الكلم, and the clause يرفعه is a ḥāl from العمل, or an explanatory resumption.]; and the fāʿil (agent) of (يرفعه) is a pronoun referring to the Divine Name [Note: Or it refers to العمل, and the third-person pronoun refers to الكلم الطيّب.], and the third-person pronoun refers to العمل; (الواو) a conjunction; (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ عذاب; (السيّئات) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its adjective [Note: And if the verb (يمكرون) is made to imply the meaning of "earn" (يكسبون), then السيّئات is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).], i.e. they plot the evil plots; (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause يبور.
The clause «من كان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان يريد ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يريد ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كان.
The clause «لله العزّة ...» has no grammatical position: a reason for the implied apodosis, i.e.:
whoever wants honour, let him seek it from Allah.
The clause «يصعد..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «العمل الصالح يرفعه..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يصعد [Note: It may be a ḥāl from الكلم.].
The clause «يرفعه ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (العمل).
The clause «الذين يمكرون..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من كان..
The clause «يمكرون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لهم عذاب..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «مكر أولئك..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «هو يبور..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ «مكر».
The clause «يبور» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).

* Rhetoric:
Metonymic figure (al-majāz al-mursal): in the words of the Exalted «إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ».
The ascent of words to Him, the Exalted, is a majāz mursal for His accepting them, by the relation of concomitance (luzūm); or a metaphor (istiʿāra) likening acceptance to ascent. It is also permissible to make الكلم a majāz for what it is written in, by the relation of containment (ḥulūl).

safi-cedvel:11-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من تراب) attached to (خلقكم), and likewise (من نطفة), as it is conjoined to the first; (أزواجا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) negative; (أنثى) genitive in form and nominative in position, the fāʿil (agent) of تحمل; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (بعلمه) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أنثى, i.e.: except accompanied by His knowledge, or except her carrying being known to Him; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) like the first; (معمّر) genitive in form, nominative in position, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (ينقص) is a pronoun referring to معمّر; (من عمره) attached to (ينقص); (إلّا في كتاب) like إلّا بعلمه, and the ḥāl is from معمّر or from عمر; (على الله) attached to (يسير).
The clause «الله خلقكم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلقكم..» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
The clause «جعلكم..» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause خلقكم.
The clause «تحمل من أنثى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «تضع ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تحمل.
The clause «يعمر من معمّر..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تحمل or to the resumption.
The clause «ينقص ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعمّر.
The clause «إنّ ذلك.. يسير» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal (taʿlīliyya).
(12) (الواو) a conjunction in the six places; (ما) negative; (سائغ) another khabar, nominative [Note: Or it is a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (شرابه), and the clause is the khabar of هذا..]; (شرابه) fāʿil of the active participle سائغ; (من كلّ) attached to (تأكلون); (فيه) attached to مواخر [Note: Or attached to (ترى).]; (اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl); (تبتغوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن after the lām; (من فضله) attached to (تبتغوا) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تبتغوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (مواخر).
The clause «ما يستوي البحران ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «هذا عذب ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
The clause «هذا ملح ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause هذا عذب.
The clause «تأكلون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما يستوي.. [Note: Or conjoined to the ḥāl clause, in the position of accusative.].
The clause «تستخرجون ...» is conjoined to the clause تأكلون and takes its grammatical status.
The clause «تلبسونها..» is in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of حلية.
The clause «ترى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «تبتغوا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the concealed particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «لعلّكم تشكرون..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied reason, i.e. that you may be provided for and that you may give thanks..
The clause «تشكرون..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(معمّر): passive participle of the four-letter verb عمّر; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Speech in which latitude is taken (al-kalām al-mutasāmaḥ fīhi): in the words of the Exalted «وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ وَلا يُنْقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ».
A human being is either long-lived (muʿammar), i.e. of long life, or of diminished life, i.e. short; as for long life and its opposite succeeding one another upon him, that is impossible. Therefore His words «وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ وَلا يُنْقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ» are sound, for this is speech in which latitude is taken, trusting the listeners' understanding to interpret it, and relying on their intellects to direct its meaning aright, and that the impossibility of length and shortness in one life will not be confused for them. The widespread speech of people is on this [pattern]. They say:
"Allah does not reward a servant nor punish him except rightfully." And: "I never enjoyed a land nor found it unwholesome except that my stay in it was short", i.e.: I disliked residing in it.
2- Representative simile (al-tamthīl): in the words of the Exalted «وَما يَسْتَوِي الْبَحْرانِ».
Some call it the representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya). It is a construction used outside its [original] place, by the relation of resemblance, with no mention in it of the thing likened nor of the particle of comparison. This is an example that clarifies it, namely their saying:
"You are striking cold iron": you have likened the state of one who insists on obtaining something whose realization is impossible to the state of one who strikes cold iron, the common factor being that each of them is an action from which no effect is hoped for. In this construction there is no mention of the thing likened nor of the particle of comparison, so it is a representative metaphor, because it is a construction used for other than what it was coined for, and the resemblance between the figurative and the literal meanings is evident. This type is frequent in current proverbs in prose and poetry, like their saying: «إن كنت ريحا فقد لاقيت إعصارا» ("If you are a wind, you have met a whirlwind"), applied to one who presumes against you, or to a strong person who falls upon one stronger and more violent than him. The one addressed was not a wind, nor did he meet a whirlwind.

safi-cedvel:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(في النهار) attached to (يولج), and likewise (في الليل); and the fāʿil (agent) of يولج in both places, and the fāʿil of (سخر), refers to Allah; (لأجل) attached to (يجري); and the reference in (ذلكم) is to the One described by the preceding attributes; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its first khabar (predicate) being الله and its second khabar ربّكم; (له) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ الملك.. and the clause is a third khabar; (الواو) a conjunction; (من دونه) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied object of تدعون; (ما) negative; (قطمير) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «يولج الليل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يولج النهار ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «سخّر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «كلّ يجري..» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from الشمس and القمر.
The clause «يجري..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ) [Note: (كلّ) comes as a mubtadaʾ with an intended annexation, i.e. each one of them, so the tanwīn in it is a compensation for a word.].
The clause «ذلكم الله ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «الذين تدعون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ذلكم الله.
The clause «تدعون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ما يملكون..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
(14) (لا) negative; (يسمعوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (ما) negative; (لكم) attached to (استجابوا); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يكفرون), and likewise (بشرككم); (الواو) resumptive; (لا) negative ...
The clause «تدعوهم ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) — or an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا يسمعوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis, not joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «سمعوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تدعوهم.
The clause «ما استجابوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يكفرون..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تدعوهم.
The clause «لا ينبّئك مثل خبير..» has no grammatical position: resumptive..

* Morphology:
(قطمير): a noun for the husk that envelops the date-stone.. or it is the cleft of the date-stone — the choice of al-Mubarrad. Its pattern is فعليل.

* Benefits:
Among the types of (لو):
Among the types of (لو) is that in which no suitable connection between the two parts is conceivable. It is of two kinds:
1- That in which what is intended is to affirm the apodosis whether the condition is present or absent, though with its absence it is more fitting. That is like the report (athar) from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "What an excellent servant Ṣuhayb is! Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him." It indicates the affirmation of non-disobedience in every case, and that the absence of disobedience together with the presence of fear is more fitting. It does not indicate the negation of the apodosis for two reasons:
The first: that its indicating that is only by way of contrary implication (mafhūm al-mukhālafa). In this report, the congruent implication (mafhūm al-muwāfaqa) indicated non-disobedience, because if disobedience is absent when there is no fear, then with fear it is more fitting; and when these two implications conflict, the congruent implication is given precedence.
The second: since suitability is absent, causality is absent, so lack of fear was not made the cause of non-disobedience. Thus we know that non-disobedience is caused by another matter, namely modesty (ḥayāʾ) and reverence, and that continues along with fear. So non-disobedience when there is no fear rests on that cause alone, and when there is fear it rests on it only, or on it and on fear. On that basis is explained the verse of Luqmān وَلَوْ أَنَّما فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلامٌ وَالْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ ما نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ, because the intellect is certain that if the words are not exhausted with the abundance of these things, then that they are not exhausted with their scarcity is more fitting. Likewise in the verse we are dealing with, وَلَوْ سَمِعُوا مَا اسْتَجابُوا لَكُمْ, because non-response when there is no hearing is more fitting; and likewise وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ لَتَوَلَّوْا, for turning away when there is no making-to-hear is more fitting.
2- That the apodosis is affirmed in every case, without any reference to what is more fitting, e.g. (وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعادُوا لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ). In this and its like, its being established is known through another cause continuing under both suppositions. What is intended in this kind is to establish the occurrence of the second [part]; as for the impossibility in the first, even though it obtains, it is not what is intended.
It becomes clear from this that the view of whoever says that (لو) is "a particle of impossibility because of impossibility" is unsound, and that the good expression is that of Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on him: "a particle for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else".

safi-cedvel:15-18.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أيها الناس) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (3) of this sūra.]; (إلى الله) attached to الفقراء; (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); (الغنيّ) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الله.
The clause «يا أيها الناس ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنتم الفقراء ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «الله.. الغنيّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
(16) (بخلق) attached to (يأت)..
The clause «يشأ ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the vocative.
The clause «يذهبكم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «يأت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يذهبكم.
(17) (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) negative, operating like ليس; (على الله) attached to عزيز; (عزيز) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar of ما.
The clause «ما ذلك.. بعزيز» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يشأ.
(18) (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative; (وازرة) fāʿil (agent), nominative, with an omitted described noun, i.e. "a burden-bearing soul"; (وزر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (أخرى) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, and with an omitted described noun, i.e. "another soul"; (مثقلة) fāʿil of تدع, and with an omitted described noun, i.e. "a heavily laden soul"; (إلى حملها) attached to (تدع), and the object of تدع is omitted, i.e. a soul calls a soul; (لا) negative; (يحمل) an imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis, passive; (منه) attached to (يحمل); (شيء) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle, and the noun (ism) of (كان) is a pronoun referring to the one called upon, understood from the context of the speech; (ذا) khabar of كان, accusative [Note: Al-ʿUkbarī permitted that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of complete (tāmma) كان.]; (إنّما) the restraining and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (بالغيب) a ḥāl from the object — or the agent —; (الواو) resumptive — or a conjunction —; (تزكّى) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (إنّما) like the first; (لنفسه) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يتزكّى; (الواو) a conjunction; (إلى الله) a fronted khabar....
The clause «لا تزر وازرة..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يشأ.
The clause «تدع مثقلة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يشأ.
The clause «لا يحمل منه شيء..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis, not joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «كان ذا قربى ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «إنّما تنذر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يخشون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أقاموا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «من تزكّى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّما تنذر ...
The clause «تزكّى ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يتزكى ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis..
The clause «إلى الله المصير ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من تزكّى.

* Morphology:
(18) مثقلة: feminine of مثقل, passive participle of the four-letter verb أثقل; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(حملها): a noun for what is carried; the plural is أحمال on the pattern أفعال, [and] حمولة on the pattern فعولة with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha): in the words of the Exalted «أَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ».
He made الفقراء definite to exaggerate their poverty, as though, because of the greatness of their want and the intensity of their need, they alone are the poor, and as though the want of all other creatures, relative to their poverty, is as nothing.
Therefore the Exalted said «وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ ضَعِيفاً».
2- Derivational paronomasia (jinās al-ishtiqāq): in the words of the Exalted «وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى».
The paronomasia is between تزر, وازرة and وزر. Al-wizr, as in al-Miṣbāḥ, is sin. Al-wizr is also a heavy load; from it one says وزر يزر, of the bāb of وعد, when one bears sin.

safi-cedvel:19-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation, in the five places [Note: It was said that they are redundant before (النور، الحرور، الأموات), and not redundant before (الظلمات، الظلّ), because these two are agents of two omitted verbs.]; (الظلمات، النور الظل، الحرور) words conjoined by conjunctions to الأعمى and البصير, each with what corresponds to it; (ما) like the first; (الأموات) conjoined to الأحياء; (ما), the third, negative, operating like ليس; (مسمع) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar (predicate) of ما; (في القبور) attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila (relative clause) of من.
(إن) negative; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (نذير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) أنت.
The clause «ما يستوي الأعمى..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما يستوي الأحياء..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «إنّ الله يسمع..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يسمع من يشاء ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يشاء..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «ما أنت بمسمع..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّ الله يسمع.
The clause «إن أنت إلّا نذير..» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) —

* Morphology:
(الحرور): maṣdar (verbal noun) of حرّ يحرّ, of the bāb of ضرب and the bāb of نصر, and it is the intensity of the heat of the sun and other things; or it is a noun for the hot wind. Abū ʿUbayda said:
Ruʾba informed us that al-ḥarūr is by day and al-samūm by night. The word is feminine; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Representative simile and antithesis (al-tamthīl wa-l-ṭibāq): in the words of the Exalted «الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ».
A likeness for the believer and the disbeliever; and the darkness and the light, a likeness for truth and falsehood; and likewise the shade and the scorching heat, and the living and the dead, a likeness for those who entered Islam and those who did not enter it and persisted in disbelief.

safi-cedvel:24-26.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its noun (ism); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object or from the agent; (بشيرا) a ḥāl from the object, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (إن) a particle of negation; (أمّة) genitive in form, nominative in position, mubtadaʾ (subject) — supported by a negation —; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (فيها) attached to (خلا).
The clause «إنّا أرسلناك..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرسلناك..» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «إن من أمّة إلّا خلا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «خلا فيها نذير..» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أمّة..).
(25) (الواو) a conjunction; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (من قبلهم) attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; (بالبيّنات) attached to a ḥāl from رسلهم; (بالزبر، بالكتاب) both attached to what the first preposition-phrase is attached to.
The clause «يكذّبوك..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّا أرسلناك.
The clause «قد كذّب الذين..» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «جاءتهم رسلهم..» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the relative noun.
(26) (الفاء) a conjunction; (كيف) an interrogative noun for affirmation (taqrīr), in the position of accusative as khabar of كان; (نكير) the noun of كان, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted to suit the verse-endings (fawāṣil).. and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «أخذت..» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause كذّب الذين..
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كان نكير..» is conjoined to the clause أخذت الذين.. because the interrogation here is affirmative (taqrīrī), i.e.: I punished those who disbelieved, and My disapproval was in its proper place ...

safi-cedvel:27-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for affirmative interrogation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī); (من السماء) attached to (أنزل) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ماء.]; (به) attached to (أخرجنا), and (الباء) is causal; (مختلفا) naʿt (adjective) of ثمرات, accusative; (ألوانها) fāʿil (agent) of the active participle (مختلفا); (الواو) a conjunction; (من الجبال) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) جدد; (بيض، حمر، مختلف) adjectives of جدد, nominative like it; (ألوانها), the second, fāʿil of the active participle مختلف; (غرابيب) conjoined to بيض [Note: Or to جدد.]; (سود) a badal (substitute) of غرابيب, or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) with the intention of emphasis.
The clause «تر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنزل....» is in the position of nominative as khabar of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الله أنزل ...) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ترى.
The clause «أخرجنا..» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أنزل [Note: And in the speech there is iltifāt (a shift) from the third-person pronoun to the first person.].
The clause «من الجبال جدد ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
(28) and (الواو) a conjunction; (من الناس) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ مختلف, with an omitted described noun, i.e. "a kind differing in its colours"..; (ألوانه) fāʿil of the active participle مختلف; (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) governed by مختلف; (إنّما) the restraining and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (الله) the Divine Name, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من عباده) attached to a ḥāl from the postponed fāʿil العلماء ...
The clause «من الناس ... مختلف ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «يخشى الله ... العلماء..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله عزيز ...» has no grammatical position, having the status of a reason (taʿlīl).

* Morphology:
(جدد): plural of جدّة, a noun for a track; some said it is a singular meaning the clear road, and the singular has been put in the place of the plural.. The pattern of جدّة is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn, and the pattern of جدد is فعل, with ḍamma then fatḥa.
(بيض): plural of أبيض, on the pattern أفعل, a noun for the well-known colour or an adjective for it. The original of بيض is to be on the pattern فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn — its singular being أفعل — then the bāʾ was given kasra to suit the yāʾ, so one says بيض.
(حمر): plural of أحمر, on the pattern أفعل; the pattern of حمر is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, the regular (qiyāsī) plural of an adjective on أفعل.
(غرابيب): plural of غربيب, a noun meaning jet-black, extreme in blackness; its pattern is فعليل with kasra on the fāʾ, and the pattern of غرابيب is فعاليل.
(سود): plural of أسود, on the pattern أفعل; the pattern of سود is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, and the plural is regular, like بيض and حمر.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift): in the words of the Exalted «فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ».
He shifted from the third person to the first person to show the perfection of His care for the act, because of the wonderful workmanship in it, which tells of the perfection of power and wisdom.
2- Al-tadbīj (colour-weaving): in the words of the Exalted «وَمِنَ الْجِبالِ جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُها وَغَرابِيبُ سُودٌ».
Al-tadbīj is that the speaker mentions colours, intending by them metonymy, and by mentioning them allusion (tawriya), for things of description, praise, satire, love-poetry or other such arts. By this Allah intended a metonymy for roads that are unclear, because the white highway is the road which has been travelled very much; it is the clearest and most evident of roads, in which the one who strays off course is safe, and the one who goes deep in journeys, and who persists in lying on the ground of caves, does not fear crossing it. Therefore it was said: "He led them on the white highway." Below it is the red, and below the red the black, as though it, in its obscurity and the confusion of its landmarks, is the opposite of the white in manifestness and clarity. Since these three colours, in their manifestness to the eye, are two extremes and a middle between them — the upper extreme in manifestness being white, the lower extreme in obscurity being black, and red between them, according to the arrangement of colours and compositions — and since the colours of mountains do not, for the most part, go beyond these three colours, the noble verse came with this division. So tadbīj occurs in it, together with soundness of division (ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm). It is set out in a familiar pattern, presented for taking account of the blessings, in that to which they guide of striving in pursuit of benefits and advantages, and avoiding the perils and destructions of this world and the Hereafter.
3- Turning to the nominal [clause] (al-ʿudūl ilā al-ismiyya): in the words of the Exalted «وَمِنَ النَّاسِ» and in His words before it «وَمِنَ الْجِبالِ»: the two clauses are brought as nominal clauses, despite their sharing with the verbal clause before them in adducing their content as evidence of people's diversity in inner states, because the difference of mountains, people, beasts and cattle in the colours mentioned is a continuing matter, so it was expressed by what indicates continuity; whereas the bringing forth of varied fruits, since it is an occurring (ḥādith) matter, was expressed by what indicates occurrence.
4- Fronting, postponing and restriction (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr wa-l-ḥaṣr): in the words of the Exalted «إِنَّما يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبادِهِ الْعُلَماءُ», to restrict fear to the scholars, as though it were said: those among His servants who fear Allah are the scholars, not others. But if you fronted the agent, the meaning would turn into: they fear none but Allah. These are two different meanings, as appears to one who reflects.

* Benefits:
1- The government of the ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the active participle):
The active participle indicates a temporary quality in a person, such as سابح (swimming), لاعب (playing). As for the ṣifa mushabbaha, it indicates a fixed quality, such as كريم, شجاع, صلب.. etc. Both the active participle and the passive participle, when they indicate fixed qualities in a person, are treated as the ṣifa mushabbaha; so the active participle in the verse مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُهُ indicates a ṣifa mushabbaha.
As for the government of the ṣifa mushabbaha: its governed word is either nominative as an agent, as in the noble verse مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُهُ — ألوانه being the fāʿil of the ṣifa mushabbaha مختلف —; or genitive by annexation, e.g. (أخوك حسن الصوت), which is its most frequent state; or accusative as tamyīz (specification) if it is indefinite, or as quasi-object if it is definite, e.g. (أخوك حسن صوتا) (أخوك حسن صوته). If the ṣifa mushabbaha is made definite by (ال), then its governed word, when annexed to it, must be made definite by (ال) or be annexed to what is definite by (ال), e.g. (أخوك الحسن الصوت) and (أخوك الحسن أداء النشيد).
2- Knowledge refines thought and conduct:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: the meaning of the verse is: "Only those of My creation fear Me who know My might, My honour and My authority." Whoever increases in knowledge increases in fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
From ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did something and allowed it, and some people abstained from it. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he delivered a sermon, praised Allah, then said: "What is the matter with people who abstain from a thing that I do? By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of them about Allah and the most intense of them in fear of Him." And from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon the like of which I never heard, and said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, you would not take pleasure in your wives on the beds, and you would go out to the ṣuʿudāt (the roads) beseeching (calling upon Allah)." So the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ covered their faces, with a khanīn [coming from them]. Al-khanīn is weeping with a nasal sound and drawing the voice through the nose.
Masrūq said: "Fear of Allah suffices as knowledge, and being deluded about Allah suffices as ignorance." And Muqātil said: "The people most intense in fear of Allah are the most knowledgeable of them."

safi-cedvel:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(ممّا) attached to (أنفقوا), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "We provided them with it" (رزقناهم إيّاه); (سرّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar [Note: Or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial).], since it is its kind..
The clause «إنّ الذين ... يرجون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يتلون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أقاموا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أنفقوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «رزقناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يرجون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ [Note: Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that the khabar be the clause (إنّه غفور), with the linking pronoun implied, i.e.: forgiving to them.. and the clause يرجون is a ḥāl from the agent in (أنفقوا).].
The clause «لن تبور..» is in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of تجارة.
(30) (اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl) — or the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba) —; (يوفّيهم) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن after the lām; (يزيدهم) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يوفّيهم); (من فضله) attached to (يزيدهم) [Note: And it is in the place of the second object.]....
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يوفّيهم..) is in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted [verb], i.e. "they did that so that He may pay them in full".. or attached to (يرجون) if the lām is the lām of consequence.
The clause «يوفّيهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the concealed particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يزيدهم..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يوفّيهم..
The clause «إنّه غفور ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:31-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الذي) a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being الحقّ; (إليك) attached to (أوحينا); (من الكتاب) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied returning pronoun [Note: It may be attached to (أوحينا), with (من) for the genus or partitive.]; (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); (مصدّقا) an emphasizing ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), accusative; (لما) attached to (مصدّقا) [Note: Or the lām is redundant, for strengthening, and (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle (مصدقا).]; (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (بعباده) attached to خبير and بصير; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (بصير) a second khabar of إنّ, nominative.
The clause «الذي أوحينا.. الحقّ..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله.. لخبير..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(32) (الذين) a relative noun in the position of accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi, by the verb's being made to imply the meaning of "We gave" (أعطينا), and (الكتاب) is the second object; (من عبادنا) attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun; (الفاء) a conjunction of ramification (tafrīʿiyya); (منهم) attached to an omitted fronted khabar, in the three places, for the mubtadaʾs (ظالم، مقتصد، سابق); (لنفسه) attached to ظالم [Note: The lām may be redundant, for strengthening, so (نفسه) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the mafʿūl bihi of the active participle ظالم.]; (بالخيرات) attached to سابق; (بإذن) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in سابق [Note: Or attached to سابق.]; (ذلك) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ [Note: The reference is to the outstripping or to the bequeathing of the Book.]; (هو) a separating pronoun [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a second mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is الفضل, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.]; (الفضل) khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك..
The clause «أورثنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «اصطفينا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «منهم ظالم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصطفينا..
The clause «منهم مقتصد..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصطفينا..
The clause «منهم سابق ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصطفينا..
The clause «ذلك.. الفضل..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
(33) (جنّات) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يدخلونها.. or it is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.]; and (الواو) in (يحلّون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (فيها) attached to a ḥāl from the agent; (من أساور) attached to (يحلّون); (من ذهب) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أساور; (لؤلؤا) mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being يحلّون; (فيها) attached to a ḥāl from حرير — an adjective that has preceded the noun it qualifies —.
The clause «(هو) جنّات ...» has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) of (ذلك هو الفضل).
The clause «يدخلونها ...» is in the position of nominative as naʿt of جنّات — or a ḥāl from it —.
The clause «يحلّون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the agent of يدخلونها or from the object [Note: Or it is a second khabar of جنّات if that is parsed as a mubtadaʾ.].
The clause «لباسهم فيها حرير» is conjoined to the clause يحلّون.
(34) (الواو) resumptive; (لله) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الحمد; (الذي) a relative noun in the position of genitive as naʿt of the Divine Name; (عنّا) attached to (أذهب); (اللام) the shifted lām, for emphasis ...
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الحمد لله ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «أذهب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «إنّ ربّنا لغفور..» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
(الذي) a badal of the first relative noun, in the position of genitive; (من فضله) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of أحلّنا; (لا) negative; (فيها) attached to (يمسّنا) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from نصب, or a ḥāl from the object pronoun in (يمسّنا).]; (لا يمسّنا فيها لغوب) like لا يمسّنا فيها نصب.
The clause «أحلّنا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
The clause «لا يمسّنا ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the first or the second object.
The clause «لا يمسّنا (the second)» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يمسّنا (the first).

* Morphology:
(35) المقامة: a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun with prefixed mīm) of the four-letter verb أقام; its pattern is مفعلة, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn, and the (التاء) is added for intensification.
(لغوب): maṣdar of لغب, of the bāb of نصر, meaning "to be tired", or of the bāb of فتح or the bāb of كرم; it was also said to be of the bāb of فرح, but that is a weak dialect. Its pattern is فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ. There are other maṣdars from the first three bābs, namely لغب with fatḥa then sukūn, and لغوب with fatḥa on the lām; and from the last bāb لغب with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the words of the Exalted «ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا».
A dependent (tabaʿiyya) implicit metaphor: He likened the giving of the Book to them, without toil or fatigue in its reaching them, to the inheritance received by an heir.

* Benefits:
- The categories of Muslims:
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite this verse (ثم أورثنا الكتاب) up to His words (ومنهم سابق بالخيرات), and he said: "As for the one who outstrips in good deeds, he will enter Paradise without reckoning; as for the moderate one, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning; and as for the one who wrongs himself, he will be held at the Standing until grief enters him, then he will enter Paradise." Then he recited this verse: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ إِنَّ رَبَّنا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ.
It was also said: the outstripper is one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, the moderate one is one whose good and bad deeds are equal, and the wrongdoer is one whose bad deeds outweigh his good deeds. If you say: why did He put the wrongdoer first, then the moderate, then the outstripper? Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq said: He began with the wrongdoers to make known that one does not draw near to Him except by His generosity and that wrongdoing does not affect the choosing; then He put the moderate second because they are between fear and hope; then He ended with the outstrippers so that no one would feel secure from His plan, and all of them are in Paradise. It was also said: He ordered them in this order according to people's stations, because the states of servants are three: disobedience and heedlessness, then repentance. When a man disobeys he enters the domain of the wrongdoers; when he repents he enters the company of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving are abundant, he enters the number of the outstrippers.
It was also said: He put the wrongdoer first because of the abundance and prevalence of wrongdoing; then the moderate are few in comparison with the wrongdoers, and the outstrippers fewer than the few, so for this reason He put them last. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best what He intends and the secrets of His Book.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) نار; (لا) negative; (عليهم) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive (يقضى); (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); (يموتوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن after the fāʾ; (لا) like the first; (عنهم) nāʾib fāʿil of the passive يخفّف [Note: The nāʾib fāʿil may be (من عذابها), and (عنهم) attached to (يخفّف).]. (من عذابها) attached to (يخفّف)..
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يموتوا ...) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the preceding negation, i.e.: there is no decree upon them, and so another death («فموت آخر») [Translator's note: Translated as written; the sense is that there is no decree of death upon them and hence no death.].
(كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) governed by نجزي..
The clause «الذين كفروا....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لهم نار ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «لا يقضى عليهم..» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (لهم), what governs it being the [implied] "being established" (al-istiqrār).].
The clause «يموتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the concealed particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «لا يخفّف عنهم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يقضى..
The clause «نجزي ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical..
(37) (الواو) a conjunction; (فيها) attached to (يصطرخون); (ربّنا) the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative, with the vocative particle omitted from it; (نعمل) an imperfect verb, jussive, the response to the request; (صالحا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its adjective [Note: Or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.]; (غير) naʿt (adjective) of (صالحا) [Note: Or a second naʿt of the omitted [noun] which is the mafʿūl muṭlaq, or the mafʿūl bihi.]; (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) an indefinite noun qualified [by an adjective] (nakira mawṣūfa) meaning "a time", attached to (نعمّركم); (فيه) attached to the verb يتذكّر; (من) a relative noun, fāʿil (agent) of يتذكّر; (الواو) a conjunction — or circumstantial —; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition, and the second is causal; (ما) negative; (للظالمين) attached to a fronted khabar; (نصير) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «هم يصطرخون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يخفّف عنهم.
The clause «يصطرخون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The vocative clause «ربّنا..» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech) of an implied saying.
The clause «أخرجنا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «نعمل ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «كنّا نعمل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «نعمل ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنّا.
The clause «نعمّركم..» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the implied object of speech, i.e.: it will be said to them: Did We not give you respite and prolong your life ...
The clause «يتذكّر ...» is in the position of accusative as naʿt of (ما).
The clause «تذكّر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «جاءكم النذير..» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause نعمّركم [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl, with قد implied.].
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you disbelieved in the warner, then taste.
The clause «ما للظالمين من نصير..» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(يصطرخون): it contains the replacement (ibdāl) of the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form by ṭāʾ. Its origin is يصترخون; the tāʾ came after the ṣād, so it was changed into ṭāʾ by a regular (qiyāsī) change. Its pattern is يفتعلون.

* Benefits:
- غير:
غير: a noun that is necessarily annexed in meaning; it may be cut off from annexation in wording if the meaning is understood and the word ليس precedes it. Their saying (لا غير) is a solecism and an error. One says: (قبضت عشرة ليس غيرها), with غير in the nominative on the omission of the khabar, i.e. "received", and with it in the accusative on the concealment of the noun [of ليس], i.e. (ليس المقبوض غيرها). And (ليس غير) with fatḥa without tanwīn, also on the concealment of the noun, with the muḍāf ilayhi omitted in wording but intended to be present; and (ليس غير) with ḍamma without tanwīn.
«غير» does not become definite by annexation, because of the intensity of its vagueness. «غير» annexed in wording is used in two ways:
The first — and it is the basic one — is that it be an adjective of an indefinite noun, as in the words of the Exalted in the verse we are dealing with رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا نَعْمَلْ صالِحاً غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ, or of a definite noun close to it, as in the words of the Exalted صِراطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ. غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ, because what is made definite generically is close to the indefinite, and because غير, when it occurs between two opposites, its vagueness is weakened.
The second: that it be [for] exception, so it is parsed with the i'rab of the noun occurring after (إلا). We have spoken about that in detail in another place, so let it be consulted.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(بذات) attached to عليم.
The clause «إنّ الله عالم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنه عليم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأرض) attached to خلائف; (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause كفر; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (عليه) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ كفره; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative; (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يزيد) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (مقتا).]; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (مقتا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا يزيد ... إلّا خسارا) like the preceding..
The clause «هو الذي..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جعلكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «من كفر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفر ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «عليه كفره» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «لا يزيد ... كفرهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «لا يزيد.. كفرهم (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].

* Morphology:
(خلائف): plural of خليفة, a noun for one who succeeds another; the word is masculine and the tāʾ is for intensification. Its pattern is فعيلة, and its verb is خلف يخلف, of the bāb of نصر.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation, and the seeing in the verb is visual; (الذين) a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of شركاء; (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied returning pronoun, i.e. "you call upon them besides Allah"; (ماذا) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by خلقوا [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), (ذا) a relative noun, khabar (predicate), and the clause خلقوا ... is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.]; (من الأرض) attached to a ḥāl from the interrogative noun; (أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the hamza; (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ شرك; (في السموات) attached to a naʿt of شرك; (أم) like the first; (كتابا) second mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) a conjunction; (على بيّنة) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم; (منه) attached to a naʿt of بيّنة; (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (إن) a particle of negation; (بعضهم) a badal (substitute) of the fāʿil (agent), nominative; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (غرورا) second mafʿūl bihi [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its kind; and it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).], accusative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرأيتم ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «تدعون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أروني ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) within the scope of the speech [Note: Or it is a badal of the object of speech.].
The clause «خلقوا ...» is in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi of the verb of seeing, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogation.
The clause «لهم شرك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آتيناهم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم على بيّنة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتيناهم.
The clause «يعد الظالمون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تزولا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and it is complete (tāmm); (والألف) [the alif] is the fāʿil (agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تزولا ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "out of aversion to their ceasing" [Note: Or in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (يمسك), i.e. He holds them from ceasing, i.e. He prevents them from ceasing (al-Zajjāj).].
(الواو) a conjunction; (اللام) paving the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (زالتا) in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (إن) negative; (أحد) genitive in form, nominative in position, fāʿil of أمسكهما; (من بعده) attached to (أمسكهما); (غفورا) a second khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative.
The clause «إنّ الله يمسك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يمسك ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تزولا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «زالتا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «إن أمسكهما من أحد» has no grammatical position: the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) ...
And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «إنه كان حليما ...» has no grammatical position: a causal resumption.
The clause «كان حليما ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:42-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (بالله) attached to (أقسموا), and the pronoun in it refers to the disbelievers of Makka; (جهد) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its kind — or its adjective — [Note: Or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial).]; (اللام) paving the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن جاءهم) like إن زالتا [Note: In verse (41) of this sūra.]; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يكوننّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters is the noun (ism) of يكونن, and (النون) is for emphasis; (أهدى) khabar (predicate) of يكوننّ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa; (من إحدى) attached to (أهدى); (الفاء) a conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb meaning [when], implying the sense of condition, attached to the negated (زادهم) [Translator's note: The source has «بمعن», evidently a truncated «بمعنى حين» ("meaning 'when'").]; (ما) negative; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (نفورا) second object.
The clause «أقسموا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إن جاءهم نذير ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يكوننّ أهدى ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the oath ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «جاءهم نذير ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «ما زادهم إلّا نفورا..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of the non-jussive condition.
(43) (استكبارا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "being arrogant" — al-Akhfash —, or it is a badal (substitute) of (نفورا).]; (في الأرض) attached to (استكبارا); (الواو) a conjunction; (مكر) conjoined to (استكبار) — or to (نفورا) —; (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl — or parenthetical —; (لا) negative; (إلّا) for restriction; (بأهله) attached to (يحيق); (الفاء) a conjunction; (هل) an interrogative particle for negation; (إلّا) like the first; (سنّة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (لسنّة) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تجد [Translator's note: The source has «عمله», evidently for «عامله» ("its governor").]; (الواو) a conjunction; (لن تجد.. تحويلا) like the preceding.
The clause «لا يحيق المكر ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl — or parenthetical, with no grammatical position —.
The clause «هل ينظرون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis..
The clause «لن تجد ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. whatever you do, you will not find ...
The clause «لن تجد (the second)» is conjoined to the clause لن تجد (the first).
(44) (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (الواو) a conjunction; (في الأرض) [attached] to (يسيروا) [Note: Or to a ḥāl from the agent..]; (الفاء) a conjunction; (ينظروا) jussive, conjoined to (يسيروا); (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as khabar of كان; (من قبلهم) attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (منهم) attached to أشدّ; (قوّة) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (يعجزه) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن after the lām; (شيء) genitive in form, nominative in position, fāʿil (agent) of يعجزه; (في السموات) attached to (يعجزه) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of شيء.]; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (في الأرض) attached to what (في السموات) is attached to, being conjoined to it; (قديرا) a second khabar..
The clause «لم يسيروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied [clause], i.e. "did they sit in their dwellings and not travel".
The clause «ينظروا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لم يسيروا.
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb of looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogation.
The clause «كانوا أشدّ ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, with قد implied.
The clause «ما كان الله ليعجزه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعجزه من شيء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the concealed particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعجزه ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to the omitted khabar of كان.
The clause «إنّه كان عليما» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —.
The clause «كان عليما ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(استكبارا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the six-letter verb استكبر; its pattern is استفعال, with kasra on the third letter.

* Rhetoric:
Harmony of wording with meaning (iʾtilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā): in the words of the Exalted «وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ».
The device of harmony of wording with meaning, i.e. that the words of the intended meaning suit one another, with no word in them that is out of tune with its sisters, unfitting for its place, or [rather] characterized by good neighbourliness; such that if the meaning is purely rare (gharīb), its words are purely rare, and vice versa. Since all the words adjoining the oath in this verse are of common, current usage, no rare word came in it that would need to be adjoined by something matching it in rarity.
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in the words of the Exalted «ما زادَهُمْ إِلَّا نُفُوراً».
A figurative attribution, because he was the cause of their increasing themselves in aversion to the truth and distance from it, like the words of the Exalted «فَزادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إِلَى رِجْسِهِمْ».
Coining a proverb (irsāl al-mathal): in the words of the Exalted «وَلا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ».
This is of the coining of a proverb. Among the proverbs of the Arabs: «من حفر لأخيه جبا وقع فيه منكبا» ("Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it headlong").

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. كسبوه.]; (ما) negative; (على ظهرها) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from دابة [Note: Or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi if (ترك) is transitive to two objects.], and the (الهاء) in ظهرها refers to the earth in the previous verse ...; (دابّة) genitive in form, accusative in position, object.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما كسبوا..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يؤاخذ).
(الواو) a conjunction; (لكن) for rectification (istidrāk); (إلى أجل) attached to (يؤخّرهم); (الفاء) a conjunction, and the second connects the apodosis; (بعباده) attached to (بصيرا), the khabar (predicate) of كان.
The clause «لو يؤاخذ الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كسبوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «ما ترك ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يؤخّرهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause].
The clause «جاء أجلهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position: a reason for the implied apodosis, i.e. He requited them with what they deserve..
The clause «كان بعباده بصيرا» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the words of the Exalted «ما تَرَكَ عَلى ظَهْرِها».
An implicit, imaginative (takhyīliyya) metaphor: He likened the earth to the beast that a person rides, then omitted the thing it is likened to, namely the beast, and kept for it something of its concomitants, namely the back. What is meant is: He would not leave upon it.
